title: [C15T1] - Australians' coffee and tea buying and drinking habits
prompt: The chart below shows the results of a survey about people's coffee and tea buying and drinking habits in five Australian cities. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The bar chart illustrates the results of a survey about coffee and tea consumption habits among residents in five Australian cities over the last four weeks.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, visiting cafés for coffee or tea was the most popular habit in four out of five cities, while purchasing fresh coffee was consistently the least common practice across all locations. Additionally, Melbourne recorded the highest percentage of café visitors, whereas Adelaide showed the lowest figures for this category.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding the most and least popular habits, café visits dominated in most cities, with Melbourne leading at 64%, followed closely by Hobart and Sydney at approximately 62% and 61% respectively. Brisbane recorded a moderately lower figure of 56%, while Adelaide had the smallest proportion at exactly 50%. In contrast, fresh coffee purchases represented the least favoured option across all five cities. Adelaide and Brisbane shared the lowest percentages at 34% each, while Sydney recorded a slightly higher figure of 44%. Melbourne and Hobart showed similar patterns, with 43% and 39% of residents respectively, buying fresh coffee.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: As for instant coffee purchases, the figures were more evenly distributed among the cities, ranging from 46% to 54%. Hobart topped this category at 54%, followed by Brisbane at 53% and Adelaide at 50%. Melbourne and Sydney recorded similar percentages, at 48% and 46% respectively, making them cities with the lowest instant coffee buying habits.
